review_method: Complete review of all 95 supplied table records: all parts, rows, captions, notes, context and available original/English fields; definitions checked for every proposed existing-tag fit. No external calls, OCR or Git operations.

candidates.label: anthropometry
candidates.definition: Historical measurements and reported classifications of human bodily dimensions or physical traits, including the source's anthropometric typologies.
includes: Cephalic indices, head-shape distributions, stature and bodily measurements.
Descriptive physical-type categories explicitly based on anthropometric observations.
excludes: Nationality or ethnicity without physical measurements or bodily-trait classification.
Clinical disease or nutritional status alone.
Endorsement or modern reclassification of the source's racial theories.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: nationality-and-ethnicity concerns nationality, ethnicity or explicit racial-group distributions. These tables instead classify head measurements and bodily traits within the population; age-and-sex and diseases do not describe that subject.

candidates.label: legal profession
candidates.definition: Lawyers, advocates and other practising legal professionals, including qualification, licensing, registration and professional establishment.
includes: Licensed or certified lawyers and advocates by place.
Legal professional admissions, certificates and practice qualifications.
excludes: Judicial caseload or court establishments alone.
Professional-school curricula alone, which remain vocational-education or higher-education.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: courts covers judicial institutions and caseload; occupations concerns population distribution by profession, not inventories of certified advocates or licence issuance. No current detailed tag identifies legal practitioners.

candidates.label: public holidays and commemorations
candidates.definition: Official or publicly observed holidays, anniversaries, festivals and commemorative occasions and their observance dates.
includes: National commemorative days and statutory holidays.
Calendars listing the occasion being celebrated or remembered.
excludes: Calendar-system equivalences and time zones, which remain calendars-and-time.
A date incidental to an unrelated table.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: calendars-and-time is defined as systems for reckoning and converting dates or time; historical-chronologies explicitly excludes a chronology confined to one well-defined substantive subject. These are lists of commemorative observances. Clarifying and widening calendars-and-time is an alternative to adding this ID.

candidates.label: route distances
candidates.definition: Distances between named places along identified transport routes or networks, including comparative or triangular distance matrices.
includes: Rail, overland or mixed-route distances and route-distance reference matrices.
excludes: Vessel mileage actually travelled as a traffic-output measure.
River length or territorial dimensions without a transport route.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: shipping already covers the maritime route tables broadly, so this is chiefly a reusable refinement rather than a reason to leave those tables untagged. It also supplies one accurate common term for mixed sea/overland route tables whose mode is not entirely specified. freight-and-transport-costs explicitly concerns money, not distance.

candidates.label: militias and volunteer forces
candidates.definition: Organised volunteer, municipal-defence or militia land forces and their units, strength and service.
includes: Volunteer corps and municipal defence forces.
Militia membership, unit organisation, reserves and equipment.
excludes: Every irregular armed group without evidence of militia or volunteer status.
Civilian police, ordinary standing-army personnel and sporting volunteer clubs.
Automatic inference of foreign-garrison rights from a member's nationality.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: army already covers land armed forces generally and therefore fits these tables. This proposed narrower detail would distinguish a recurring volunteer-corps series from regular armies, but is not essential to close a vocabulary gap.

candidates.label: riots and civil unrest
candidates.definition: Episodes of collective civil disorder, riots or violent unrest, with documented participants, casualties, damage or official responses.
includes: Riot events and damage or casualties explicitly attributed to them.
Collective disturbances without an established interstate-war or independence-movement purpose.
excludes: Military conflict casualties without civil-unrest context.
Peaceful political-party organisation or all ethnic population tables.
candidates.why_existing_tags_do_not_fit: The printed running section recorded in chapter_raw is The Korean Riots, while the short context calls this the Pingyang disaster. military-casualties would require a military-operation link, and offences-and-convictions does not describe victim totals. This is a useful candidate, but the causal link to the specific riot should be checked before assigning it.

deferred.reason: The excerpt gives walnut quantities traded from provinces but does not establish whether the relevant trade boundary is domestic or international. Horticulture is a possible commodity-subject reuse if its definition is clarified to cover orchard commodity trade; adding a walnut ID would not resolve the trade-direction uncertainty.

One textual table describes rival governmental/military groups and territorial control. This could justify a political-fragmentation or political-and-military-factions term if similar material recurs elsewhere, but army, parties and formal administrative-divisions should not be forced onto the whole table. Defer a new narrow ID pending cross-batch evidence.
